children: Deposits of commercial banks rose 15.3 per cent to ₹173.5-lakh crore in the September quarter of FY27 from ₹150.5-lakh crore a year earlier, according to an analysis of business updates released by 21 banks. On a sequential basis, deposits grew 5.2 per cent during the quarter.

The increase was aided by strong foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposit flows. However, deposit growth was not broad-based, with the share of low-cost Current and Savings Account (CASA) deposits at several lenders remaining flat or declining y-o-y. This points to continued reliance on term deposits and bulk funding.

Most banks reported quarter-on-quarter deposit growth of 4-6 per cent. Kotak Mahindra Bank was a notable outlier, with deposits rising 13.7 per cent sequentially. Banks that attracted significant FCNR(B) inflows generally reported stronger deposit growth, with HDFC Bank and South Indian Bank among those recording above-average growth.
HDFC Bank’s deposits grew 19 per cent y-o-y, outpacing its loan growth of more than 15 per cent and providing some relief on the funding front.

Despite stronger deposit mobilisation, banks continued to expand their loan books faster than deposits. Aggregate advances of the 21 banks grew 21.4 per cent y-o-y to ₹149.6-lakh crore in Q2FY27. On a sequential basis, advances rose more than 6.25 per cent, outpacing deposit growth by around one percentage point.

The surge in FCNR(B) inflows, estimated at about $137 billion, was still insufficient to materially ease pressure on banks’ funding metrics. The aggregate credit-deposit (CD) ratio rose to 86.3 per cent in the September quarter from 82 per cent a year earlier, reflecting the persistent gap between credit and deposit growth.

Of the 21 banks analysed, only HDFC Bank and Bank of India reported a decline in their CD ratios, although modestly. HDFC Bank recorded the sharper improvement, with its CD ratio easing to 95.7 per cent from 98.8 per cent a year earlier.

The stronger business momentum is also expected to reflect in the September-quarter earnings. Analysts expect banks to report healthy profit growth, supported by robust loan expansion and stable asset quality.

Lenders that attracted sizeable FCNR(B) deposits could face some pressure on net interest margins (NIMs) because of the temporary increase in funding costs. However, earnings are expected to remain supported by balance-sheet growth and contained credit costs.

title: Deposit growth gets FCNR(B) boost, yet trails credit expansion in Q2FY27
